TAB-FULL:v24p100/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p100/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p100/r2.claim: The Prophet has no assigned role in determining the Hour or investigating its timing; its endpoint belongs to God.

ZAJJAJ:v5p281/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p281/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p281/r5.claim: The Hour’s endpoint with the Lord means that the limit of knowledge about it belongs to Him.

NAHHAS:v5p146/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p146/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p146/r13.claim: Muntahāhā is nominative as the subject: the endpoint of its knowledge is with God.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r13.claim: Knowledge of the Hour ends with God; the Prophet stopped asking and said that God concealed five matters from even a near angel or a sent prophet, then cited the end of Quran 31:34.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p203/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p203/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق والمفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p203/r1.claim: The limit with the Lord is the limit of knowledge about when the Hour comes.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p203/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p203/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p203/r2.claim: He glosses this as saying that knowledge of the matter is with God.

JISHUMI:v10p7275/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r10.claim: Muntahā is the place at which something reaches its end.

JISHUMI:v10p7277/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r4.claim: The time of the Resurrection is known only to God.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r8.claim: The Prophet has no knowledge of the Hour; the endpoint of its knowledge belongs to God.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r4.claim: Knowledge of the Hour ends with God and has not been given to any created being.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r12.claim: The rebuke means the Prophet has no role in specifying the Hour; his task is only to warn those who fear it.

TABRISI:79:45-46/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:45-46/r12.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:79:45-46/r12.claim: The Hour's ultimate knowledge belongs to God alone.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#10/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#10/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#10/r1.claim: Knowledge of the Hour ends with the Lord.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r10.speaker: الزهري عن عروة بن الزبير
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r10.claim: The Prophet's frequent questioning is answered by saying the Hour's knowledge ends with God, so he is told not to seek it.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r13.claim: Only God knows when the Hour will occur, as the verses in al-A'raf and Luqman state.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r2.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r2.claim: He says the Prophet kept being asked about the Hour until these verses were revealed.

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:41-45/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:41-45/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:41-45/r4.claim: The Hour’s endpoint and knowledge belong to God.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#5/r1.claim: The endpoint of knowledge of the Hour's timing belongs to God alone.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#5/r2.claim: Alternatively, the question is rejected because the Prophet's sending as the last prophet is itself a sign of the Hour; a pause after “in what” is possible before the independent statement about its endpoint.

QASHANI:79:34-41/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:79:34-41/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:79:34-41/r6.claim: Knowledge of the Hour ends with God: knowing it requires the annihilation of one’s knowledge in divine knowledge and one’s self in God’s Self.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r7.claim: Only God knows the appointed time of the Hour; its knowledge is beyond the Prophet and all creation, as another verse says.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r8.speaker: رسول الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r8.claim: When Gabriel asked the Prophet when the Hour would come, he replied that the one asked knew no more than the asker.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish resurrection and the gathering, displaying humanity’s final fate after the preceding surahs’ full exposition; its oaths show the matter has reached its decisive climax.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r3.claim: All knowledge and affairs of the Hour end with God, and the Prophet was not commissioned to determine its exact time.

DURR-FULL:v8p413/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p413/r6.speaker: ابن جرير
DURR-FULL:v8p413/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj glosses the Hour's endpoint as God's knowledge and interprets the brief evening and morning as worldly time.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#3/r1.claim: On the preceding interpretation, knowledge of the Hour's essence, details, and timing ends with God; the Prophet's role was only to announce its approach.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#3/r2.claim: On the first interpretation, all knowledge of the Hour ends with God and no one else has any share, so the question to the Prophet is misplaced.

ELMALILI:79:42-46/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:42-46/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:42-46/r4.claim: Only God knows the Hour's full reality and all its details for everyone until it occurs; the Prophet is not charged to reveal more.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p96/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p96/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p96/r3.claim: ‘To your Lord is its end’ explains why the Prophet is not involved: knowledge of the Hour's end belongs exclusively to God.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p96/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p96/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p96/r4.claim: Al-muntaha began as the place where a journey ends, then came to mean destiny and, by extension, knowledge; an omitted noun is ‘knowledge of its time.’

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p96/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p96/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p96/r5.claim: Alternatively, its end may mean the point at which news of the Hour reaches someone.

TABATABAI:79:42-44/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:42-44/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:42-44/r7.claim: The Hour's endpoint belongs to God, so only He knows its reality, properties, and appointed time; people should not ask and the Prophet cannot answer.

TABATABAI:79:42-44/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:42-44/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:42-44/r8.claim: The verse may also mean that the Hour entails the extinction of things and causes, revealing that dominion belongs to God alone; even time cannot truly delimit it.

TABATABAI:79:46#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r3.claim: The Qummi commentary glosses the question as “when does it come?” and says its knowledge belongs to God.

TABATABAI:79:46#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r6.speaker: عائشة
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r6.claim: A report graded sound by al-Hakim says the Prophet was repeatedly asked about the Hour until these verses were revealed, after which he was not asked; the author says the context does not fit this as a reply to the Prophet's own question.

TABATABAI:79:46/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:46/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:46/r1.claim: The only direct Qur'anic temporal limit is the world's extinction and its cosmic upheaval; otherwise the Hour is described figuratively as a brief interval, including in 46:35 and 30:55–56.

TABATABAI:79:46/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:46/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:46/r2.claim: The Hour comes suddenly, as 7:187 says; this supports God's exclusive knowledge, though the argument needs further reflection to reconcile other verses.

ASAD-NOTES:79:42#n18/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:79:42#n18/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:79:42#n18/r1.claim: The Hour's 'utmost limit' is the beginning and end of all that can be known about it, as 7:187 also indicates.

BINTSHATI:v1p161/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p161/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p161/r1.claim: The Prophet’s task concerning the Hour is restricted to warning those who fear it, not announcing its time or place; Abū Ḥayyān says warning benefits such people.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:42/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:42/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:42/r3.claim: God's question means the Prophet cannot obtain this knowledge, which belongs to God alone (cf. Luqman 31:34).

STUDYQURAN:79:44/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:44/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:44/r1.claim: Only God knows when the Hour will occur, and He will manifest it at its appointed time.

STUDYQURAN:79:44/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:44/r2.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:79:44/r2.claim: When Gabriel asked about the Hour, the Prophet answered that the questioned person knows no more than the questioner.
